The app is now called ಇತಿಹಾಸ (Itihāsa). Choosing between the Rāmāyaṇa and the Mahābhārata is two chips at the top of Home and Read: a bow and arrow for the Rāmāyaṇa, the Sudarśana chakra for the Mahābhārata.
New app icon background, blending the two works' colours.

The Mahābhārata is now in the app as a second work: choose it from the chip under the greeting on Home and Read. It has the same reading, chant, search, saved verses, offline packs and daily śloka as the Rāmāyaṇa.
Two texts: Traditional Text (Kumbakonam, 96,415 verses) and Pune Text (critical edition, 73,821 verses), in 18 parvans with painted cards.
Your place, saved verses, today's śloka and the texts switched on are kept separately for each work; script letter, text size and theme apply to both.
Word-by-word meanings and links between the two texts are not available for the Mahābhārata yet.
Swipe sideways to move to the next or previous sarga: one finger in the reading view, two fingers in the chant view (one finger there still moves by verse).
Today's śloka is now a palm-leaf manuscript card, with round icons for another, save, word by word, share and open.
Home: Continue reading and Begin are now one card, with a small play icon to begin and an arrow to resume.
New look: a greeting Home, a Read tab and a floating tab bar.
Kāṇḍas are shown as temple-painting cards; tap one to pick a sarga.
Pick your script with one letter: ಅ, अ or A. Reading settings open from the sliders button.
A new app icon.
Every verse has a small word-by-word icon beside its number. Tap it to open the meanings; it is dimmed when a verse has none.
Click or tap any verse in the reading view to see its words with grammar and meanings. Traditional verses that differ a little from the Baroda verse show its analysis with a note.
The Traditional Text is now the default; the Baroda Text is optional and can be turned on in Options.
Word by word now also works on Traditional Text verses that match a Baroda verse.
Home no longer has the Editions section or the My list button; the phone tab bar has Home, Search and My.
Light is now the default look. Options has a Theme choice: Light, Dark, or Same as device.
The two texts have clearer names: Baroda Text (the Critical Edition) and Traditional Text (the Vulgate).
Options now lets you switch either text off, so lists, search and links show only the one you read. At least one stays on.
New Chant view: a full-screen reading mode with a book page and one verse at a time, text size, script and layout controls, swipes and keys. Closing it returns you to where you started.
Print and PDF of the chant view, in the script you chose. On phones the PDF is shared as a file.
New Home: verse of the day (365 verses, a different one each day, with words, metre and context), Continue reading, kāṇḍa tiles with sarga chips, My list.
Works offline once installed. Pages you have read are kept; whole kāṇḍas can be downloaded from About.
Bottom tab bar on phones, a side list of kāṇḍas on wide screens, and a Back button that never leaves the site.
Word-by-word analysis of Critical Edition verses, with dictionary senses of each word.
The traditional Vulgate as a second edition, with verse-by-verse links to the Critical Edition.
Critical Edition reader in Kannada script, Devanāgarī and IAST, with search and citations.
